text: The principal basis is to de-densify all the rooms to facilitate the segregation of residents so that during a pandemic, we can quickly impose lockdowns in a very targeted and precise manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also conducting a holistic review on these improved standards to be applied to future new dormitories, keeping in mind that every new disease outbreak can be very different from the existing one.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are always working in close consultation with MOH, with public health experts and with the various stakeholders such as employers, migrant workers themselves, dormitory operators and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to gather all of their views in coming up with the new standards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also draw on our experiences from the Quick Build Dormitories.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition to infrastructure, we are also studying how contact tracing has enabled us to more accurately identify, isolate and quarantine close contacts in the event of a public health outbreak.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There are also innovative processes and practices in dormitory management that can be adopted to improve overall standards in terms of infection prevention and control.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We expect to finalise all of these standards later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We recognise that higher standards may also result in higher costs for employers and dormitory operators.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many businesses would have locked in their costs in their existing projects and will now need time to adjust to higher migrant worker housing costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Dormitory operators may also be more cautious in bidding to build and own new dormitories, given the current uncertain demand for migrant worker housing alongside the evolving COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are studying each option very comprehensively and we will share our findings – and again, we will work with industry to get their feedback – in due course.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For existing dormitories, we will also consider how to progressively improve standards, pacing and phasing it so that the price fluctuations will not be steep and the gradient will be gradual; while ensuring competitive bed rental prices and a continuous, stable housing supply during the transition period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will update on all these in due time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Having put in place all the upstream and long-term measures explained earlier, we need to ensure that our efforts can be sustained for the longer term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Disease outbreaks will harm not just our valued workers, but disease outbreaks also have grave implications for employers, for the economy, for our resident population as a whole, and the provision of many services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is in all of our interests to make sure that we continually take good care of our migrant workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: COVID-19 provided the impetus for us to relook how we engage and support the migrant workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have to and will establish a resilient and safe support eco-system to care for them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Hazel Poa asked whether MOM has sufficient manpower to implement all of these ambitious plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also got the FAST teams come onsite to work with the migrant workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This assures them of our continued interest in preserving their well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We continue to provide holistic physical, mental and social care for them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our multi-layered strategy of regular testing and swift containment has also effectively helped to contain infections in the dormitories to the current very low levels.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This outbreak highlighted gaps in primary health care that migrant workers received pre-COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Often, migrant workers might delay or avoid seeking medical attention until the condition worsens significantly, with negative consequences for health, employment and work outcomes, both for the worker and the employer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government has since made it easier for migrant workers to access good primary healthcare.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will need to be able to sustain this for us to constantly survey and have sentinel reporting health clinics to detect public health threats early.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond this pandemic period, we will take stock of the healthcare eco-system for migrant workers residing in dormitories and other housing types, to see how we can sustain the longer term access to primary healthcare in a cost-effective and culturally-sensitive way.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, we hope that every migrant worker can be registered with a designated medical centre or GP clinic near where they live and work to foster better continuum of care and better doctor-patient relationships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In this way, we will shift beyond episodic care to better manage chronic health conditions, including mental health.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have set up a Project DAWN taskforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also introduced a seven-point mental health strategy comprising: (a) mental wellness promotion, (b) identification of at-risk patients/factors, (c) screening of mental health conditions, (d) surveillance of mental/emotional distress, (e) development and training of para-counsellors and counsellors, (f) timely escalation of care, and (g) provision of post-intervention support to complete and ensure a holistic mental health support eco-system for our migrant workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Employers remain responsible, ultimately, for providing and paying for their workers’ medical treatment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Hence, our review of primary healthcare support will also aim to keep these costs manageable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In a small minority of hospitalisation cases, employers can face large medical expenses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Again, we will provide an update later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: COVID-19 vaccination will also be made available to migrant workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: When ready – and it will be ready soon – it will be accompanied by comprehensive communications in all of their native languages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This additional layer of protection strengthens our defences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We encourage, when the time comes, all of our employers and workers to get vaccinated to create a safer living and working environment for everyone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Compared to 12, 13 months ago, we are much better equipped now to deal with the health pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Most importantly, employers and migrant workers have shown a significant amount of trust, patience and support in the measures which we have had to implement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One of the things we learnt is, that we were able to bring the COVID-19 situation in the dormitories under control because of the critical and crucial contributions of many, many volunteer networks who have helped workers overcome many of the fears and challenges that they face in Singapore, such as language barriers and the lack of social support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many NGO volunteers have helped to distribute food and care packs to our migrant workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many migrant worker volunteers have also stepped up to disseminate information to their peers in native languages and worked with MOM’s Forward Assurance and Support Teams (FAST) to deliver assistance at the dormitories.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Muthaiah Diwakaran, a volunteer ambassador with the Migrant Workers’ Centre (MWC), has been in Singapore for about 20 years and currently resides at Cochrane Lodge 2.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: He reaches out to care for his peers, takes questions on the latest worksite and dormitory measures, and encourages the workers to sign up for Gov.sg WhatsApp updates in their preferred language.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To better support and facilitate the outreach of more volunteer networks, ACE will partner key stakeholders to create a more structured eco-system to engage workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through this network, ACE will partner dormitory operators, employers and NGOs to better communicate with migrant workers, to understand their needs and work collectively together to uplift their well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The initiative under Project DAWN helps workers to identify signs of stress, help them to perform simple breathing exercises that can help them relieve their anxiety and learn where to find and access mental health support in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, we will also support ground-up volunteer activities that can promote social cohesion amongst migrant communities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For International Migrants Day last year, we brought together 24 partner organisations and 180 volunteers to celebrate at eight Recreation Centres all across Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will do more to widen the circle of community volunteers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We hope that this new engagement model will encourage migrant workers to step forward and co-create solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are always a work-in-progress and we encourage everyone who has ideas to come forward and share with us, so that we can work collectively to improve everyone's livelihoods.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And we encourage employers to give your fullest support to migrant workers who wish to serve their dormitory residents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Hazel Poa and Mr Pritam Singh asked about the enforcement of laws protecting migrant workers’ employment rights, such as cases of underpayment of salary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In general, foreign employees in Singapore are protected under the same civil and criminal laws as citizens for general crimes, employment matters, safety and health and injury claims.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We provide foreign employees with additional protection under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act or EFMA and the Employment Agencies Act or EAA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These prescribe the employers’ responsibilities for hiring foreign employees, such as supervision and proper deployment, prompt payment of salaries, provision of a safe working environment and ensuring acceptable accommodation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For the local employment agencies, we limit the fees in which they can charge workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will investigate all salary and fee-related complaints, which include underpayment of salaries, collection of kickbacks or recovering of employment costs, and excessive recruitment fees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Singh asked for the details of the number of migrant workers who were unpaid and the details of restitution made.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Penalties for the underpayment of salaries take into account the severity of the offence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For not paying the salaries that are due to them, employers could be prosecuted and they could be fined up to $10,000, jailed up to a year, or both, under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA).

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These penalties were last reviewed and raised in 2012, up from a fine of up to $5,000, or jail of six months or both.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Exploitation in any form is not fair to employees and is unacceptable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For underpayment of salaries, we will get the employers to make full restitution of salaries owed to the foreign employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The vast majority have been able to recover their salaries in full.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For wilful employers, MOM will take further enforcement actions and failure to comply will attract additional penalties, including payment of fines and serving an imprisonment sentence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Underpayment of salaries to any employee, foreign or local is not tolerated and we will not hesitate to take actions against any errant employers and parties who abet the offence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To Mr Singh's suggestion to require errant employers to pay the foreign employee a penalty amounting to six months of his salary for each instance of salary underpayment, MOM already requires such employers to make full restitution of the salary owed to the employee and pay a fine or be jailed if prosecuted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will facilitate the transfer of affected workers who want to continue to work in Singapore to a new employer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And in spite of many of these things that we have heard about, Singapore remains a very attractive destination for our migrant workers who want to come to work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, what we are trying to do is to assure workers that they can continue to stay in Singapore – because this is what they need – to earn an income when they report their employers for salary underpayment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As such, at this particular point in time, we do not see the need to require the employer to pay the employee an amount beyond what was owed to him.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One way to reduce the incidence of salary underpayment or non-payment is e-payment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For the remaining, we are in consultation with tripartite partners to extend requirements for electronic payments to more workers, including locals and work permit holders who are not living in the dormitories.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Leon Perera expressed concern, rightfully, about the recruitment process, including job advertisements, fees paid by migrant workers and if it was possible to establish direct recruitment channels.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, it is one month for each year capped at two months.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Harsher penalties will be meted out for subsequent convictions, including fines of up to $160,000 or a jail term of up to four years, or both.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, receiving or offering payment as consideration for the employment of migrant workers is also prohibited under the EAA and the EFMA Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Offenders found guilty under the EFMA Act can face a jail term of up to two years or a fine of up to $30,000, or both.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In recent years, MOM has also adopted the use of data analytics to detect anomalies and fraud in the employment patterns of migrant workers more quickly and more accurately.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This has helped us to proactively detect cases, in addition to complaints and tip-offs when we receive from NGOs, MWC ambassadors and migrant workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We encourage all parties to provide us with the different data sources so that we can triangulate better and we encourage migrant workers who are made to pay monies to their employers or any other party as a guarantee of employment, and members of the public with information to come forward on all these illegal recruitment and workplace practices to inform us immediately.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM has been educating foreign employees to report underpayment of salaries and employment kickbacks through various platforms and initiatives such as FWMOMCare app.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: During the mandatory Settling-In Programme, an orientation for first-time work permit holders, and roadshows, we will educate them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The regular presence of MOM’s FAST teams at the dormitories also allows for early detection.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Hence, foreign workers are now aware that they have multiple avenues to seek help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have not discounted this centralised job portal, as suggested by Members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: While we see that as a possible opening and option, we recognise the fact that different employers tap on various channels to recruit employees, whether it is employment agencies, employee referrals or direct hiring from source countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If we want to mandate a centralised recruitment platform for all employers, many of our businesses have given feedback that this will limit their hiring flexibility to meet their respective manpower needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, I think we have to be open to all different options.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, such a platform can reduce but not necessarily completely eliminate fees paid by migrant workers to these "unlicensed" overseas agents or middlemen, to assist with the documentation that is required or to help them link them to this platform or "licensed", so to speak, employment agencies in the source countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will constantly and continually work with stakeholders including employers, migrant workers themselves, the NGOs, the employment agencies, to explore the various suggestions that have been brought up in the past, today and moving forward, to reduce the recruitment costs incurred by migrant workers seeking a job in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Like my appeal earlier on, the support of employers, the NGOs and acceptance by workers will be crucial.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about protecting the rights of workers to safe and hygienic meals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, there are various options, including self-cooked food.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Migrant workers who face issues with access to adequate and proper food or other well-being concerns should report their cases to us at MOM.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In serious cases, we will take appropriate enforcement action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are happy to work with NGOs, dormitories operators and employers to explore different ways to ensure that our workers receive sufficient, sustainable and nutritious food.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With the outbreak in dormitories now under control, many volunteers are concerned about the strict measures that remain in place for workers residing in dormitories, even as the country moves into Phase Three.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We understand and we empathise with their needs and the need for social interaction.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At the same time, we are also concerned about the livelihoods of workers should a second wave or clusters develop in the dormitories.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are, therefore, calibrating and easing restrictions in a very carefully, controlled, safe manner, particularly given the fact that there is a lot of news about more virulent strains emerging.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Communal facilities have resumed operations in dormitories where operators have demonstrated good compliance with safe management measures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Each visit will be extended from the current three to four hours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Workers will have more time to carry out their personal errands or to do some sports.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The operational details are being worked out to keep the numbers in the community manageable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have no intention whatsoever for restrictions to be stricter than necessary or to be in place for longer than what is necessary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Because, we are dealing with the real risks posed by COVID-19, especially when we are trying to prevent cross-transmission or possible re-infection.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Hence, we appeal to all of you for your support and understanding as we continue to calibrate measures to adapt to the ever-evolving situation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are just doing our level best to make efforts to restore a sense of normalcy where it is possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In Mandarin):    In the past year, Singapore has introduced a series of measures to cope with the pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have gained valuable lessons and experience to prepare us for the next outbreak.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The MWOC will be able to provide the flexibility to tweak measures taken pre-departure and upon arrival to minimise the transmission risks of new workers arriving in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will enable us to continuously raise and enforce housing standards across various dormitory types and sizes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, we will put in place strong support systems to make these efforts sustainable, including strengthening healthcare provision and social networks for workers residing in dormitories and other housing types.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Everyone has a part to play in fighting COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With the cooperation of dormitory operators, employers, workers and the community, together we can minimise the risks of COVID-19 outbreaks and welcome the new norm.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Chairman, our efforts to build a safe and resilient migrant workforce must not stop here.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will fortify our defences through upstream measures before and when workers arrive into Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These series of safeguards will help us to better manage any risk of imported cases and to better onboard them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will raise living standards and enhance all of our processes in our dormitories to strengthen our collective ability to respond effectively and rapidly to future outbreaks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will put in place strong support systems to make these efforts sustainable over the longer term, including strengthening healthcare provision and social networks for workers residing in the different dormitories and the different housing types.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We recognise that these efforts come at a cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: On this note, I appeal and urge everyone and employers in particular, to seize this opportunity to accelerate your adoption of higher productivity and less labour-intensive industry models.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We call upon all of you, over the last one year, who have braved the storm together with us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: You have expended significant resources, significant opportunity costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We should all collectively strengthen our workforce, our workplace resilience, and to put in place robust and sustainable measures that will see us through the long haul.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Future pandemics are not a question of "if".

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Together, if we put our hearts and our minds together, we will always be ready for future pandemics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, earlier, Minister for Manpower outlined how MOM will strengthen our efforts to ensure workforce and workplace resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have made good progress in supporting our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the decade from 2009 to 2019, low-wage workers saw higher income growth than the average worker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This has helped to reduced income inequality, and bears testament to the Government's multi-layered approach to support our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Workfare Income Supplement, which the Government introduced in 2007, laid the foundations to supplement the incomes of our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It casts a wide net, covering full-time and part-time employees, as well as the self-employed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It supplements workers' wages by up to 30%, depending on income and age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On top of Workfare, we have the Progressive Wage Model, or PWM, and Workfare Skills Support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has tempered progress, we are fortunate that there has been broad-based preservation of jobs and employability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At its peak, the unemployment rate for OECD countries was 3.6%-points higher than pre-COVID-19 levels, whereas in Singapore, the increase was smaller at 1.6%-points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Such an effort has certainly supported our low-wage workers in these challenging times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But we are not out of the woods yet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Keeping our low-wage workers employed must continue to be our highest priority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And we have done so through measures like the Jobs Support Scheme, which has helped to keep our unemployment rate low.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Keeping this priority in mind, we should take careful steps to raise the wages of our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Especially in a time like this, we must not trifle with careless moves that would risk them being unemployed instead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to build on Workfare and extend the PWM to cover more workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This combination is a sustainable way to uplift our low-wage workers through better wages and work conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since January this year, security firms are no longer granted overtime exemption, or OTE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This means that a security officer can only work up to 72 overtime hours a month, instead of the previous industry norm of 95 hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While security officers would be heartened by this move, many were also concerned about the impact on their wages because many relied on overtime pay for their gross incomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More security officers also saw even higher wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What this means is that security officers can now work fewer overtime hours while maintaining their gross monthly wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am thankful to both the Labour Movement and security employers for continuing with these changes despite the current challenging business climate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Alvin Goh is one of many who have benefited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When he joined the industry in 2017, he worked six days each week, averaging 94 overtime hours a month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Goh was earning about $1,800 in gross wages then, with some additional support from Workfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, because of PWM, Mr Goh works up to 72 overtime hours a month – a significant reduction of 22 hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This means two additional rest days a month, which he uses to spend more time to rest and spend more time with family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Thanks to PWM wage increases and his progression up the PWM ladder, his gross wages today has increased by more than 50% from the $1,800 he was earning in 2017, to about $2,800 today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Besides improved working conditions, many of us have witnessed the transformation of job roles in the sector – from "jagas" who perform largely caretaking functions, to security officers who are skilled professionals, enabled by technology today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Careful implementation of the PWM has also helped to avoid negative employment effects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have seen the growth of more locals joining the sector of around 6% a year, from 2015 to 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Progressive Wages approach, with Workfare as a foundation, has benefited the security sector, employers and security officers, who have seen better career prospects, wages and work conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The story of Mr Alvin Goh and others like him, bear testament to the value of building on Workfare to adopt progressive wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers have been working hard to ensure that our low-wage workers can emerge stronger together with the rest of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Presently, our existing PWMs cover around 85,000 workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Dr Koh Poh Koon and Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked if the wages and prospects of our low-wage workers in the Food Services and Retail sectors could be uplifted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng also expressed similar sentiments recently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have been studying the extension of the PWM to more sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In my Committee of Supply speech last year, I reiterated our intention to do so when business conditions were more favourable – we were at the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Workgroup also recognises NTUC's aspirations for the PWMs to be implemented within two to three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And we have convened Tripartite Cluster committees for each of these sectors, which will recommend an implementation timeline, taking on board all stakeholders' concerns, including market conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The tripartite cluster committees will target to submit their recommendations on the timeline and other implementation details to the Government by the end of the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are confident that our local workers in the food services and retail sectors will likewise see a meaningful uplift to their wages in time to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also welcome NTUC's strong commitment to expanding the PWM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And we look forward to NTUC, bringing on board their social enterprises, such as NTUC Foodfare and Fairprice, when we expand the food Services and retail PWMs, along with other progressive employers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Even as the tripartite partners work through the details, we recognise that our approach will need to be balanced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During my consultations with the industry, many food services and retail employers supported the imperative to do more for low-wage workers in their sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the same time, we are also mindful that while some firms are doing very well, others may still be more at a nascent stage of recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, our intentions must therefore be carefully calibrated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It must be meaningful for the worker, but it must also be viable for our SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will pay close attention to the potential impact of PWM on business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government will do its part to support the transition, alongside employers and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also consult extensively with the employers and unions and be sensitive to existing industry practices, such as incentive-based wage remuneration like commissions, for example, when designing the PWM in these sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, all cleaners, security officers and landscape workers of licensed or registered cleaning, security and landscape firms benefit from being paid at least PWM wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Other companies may also employ staff in-house to perform these roles, such as hotels and F&B outlets which are not covered under existing PWMs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We intend to consult key affected sectors on a suitable timeline to move forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To the questions from Mr Louis Ng and Mr Fahmi Aliman, I wish to reinforce the Government's ambition to eventually cover all sectors with Progressive Wages, on top of Workfare as a fundamental layer of support for our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are starting in sectors with the highest proportion of low-wage workers in the workforce and identifying ways to expand beyond these sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also recognise that there are low-wage workers employed in similar occupations but distributed in other sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, we are studying practical ways to cover various occupational groups under Progressive Wages and will share more when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To the figures Mr Gerald Giam quoted yesterday, the discrepancy arises because of coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Part-time employees work fewer hours so their gross wages would naturally be lower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Similarly, for self-employed persons, the nature of their earnings and their working hours are not comparable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But let us also look at the big picture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The wages of our low-wage workers have not stagnated in the past decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have seen our efforts improve the wages of all Singaporeans and we have seen progress at the bottom 10% and the bottom 20%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The wages of our low-wage workers have not stagnated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They have gone up and we will continue to help them progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But regardless of how the numbers differ, an important point is that low-wage workers also receive the Workfare support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And in time to come, our aim is to cover them through Progressive Wages too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Nevertheless, more broadly, I thank Mr Gerald Giam for his consistent support of the PWM since 2014, I believe when he was a Non-Constituency Member of Parliament when he commented on its launch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We share similar objectives, even if our methods or approaches may differ.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Giam may have the impression that there is little risk of disemployment when higher PWM wages are mandated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is precisely because of the calibrated way in which we have rolled out PWM, negotiated with the industry and the Labour Movement, have we been able to avoid disemployment and improve wage outcomes in which the market can bear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Where feasible, the tripartite partners make positive improvements to the work conditions, as I shared earlier with the security sector, which in turn, promotes more local hiring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, it is a win for the employer, a win for the worker and also a win for the service buyer and hopefully consumers in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government stands ready to support, to ease the transition for firms, including training support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And that is why sectoral tripartite consultations are critical.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As for Mr Edward Chia, I agree when he cautioned, businesses, especially our SMEs, must be given a reasonable runway to adjust and prepare for the PWM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I also want to assure him that this is exactly how we prevent problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope that Mr Giam will appreciate the delicate balance involved and the Workgroup members who are trying hard to act responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Workgroup will also study how to ensure that wage growth in PWM sectors continues to outpace median wage growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our aim is really to narrow the wage gap amongst our workers and strengthen the cohesion in our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Uplifting our low-wage workers is a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Employers and workers must continue to be committed to job redesign and upskilling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As consumers, let us also recognise our responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened that a Government poll conducted early this year found that, even amidst the pandemic, a considerable proportion of respondents – 39% – were willing to pay more for goods and services to help low-wage workers receive higher wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Forty-two percent were neutral, while 19% were not prepared to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Though there are many Singaporeans who are willing to pay more, but we can see that the support is not so clear-cut.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As a nation, it is important that we stand in solidarity with our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I urge all Members in this House, across parties, to help build consensus among Singaporeans that this is but a small price to bear together for a fairer and more cohesive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the same time, the extension of PWM to these sectors is not an excuse for companies to indiscriminately raise prices, which Dr Koh and Mr Singh are rightly concerned about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the expansion of PWM to the public-facing retail and food services sectors, we will study options with relevant agencies to keep a close watch on indiscriminate profiteering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To Mr Singh's specific query on lift maintenance contracts, today, there is no requirement for Town Councils to procure services from any particular firm, though I recognise that some firms specialise in particular lift models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Authorised dealers are required to supply parts to other players on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Town Councils can also compare prices between firms to make informed decisions on awarding of contracts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Agencies will look into any unjustified contract hikes and Mr Singh can offer us details to follow-up if there are.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More broadly, Mr Singh's example brings to bear two points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But at the same time, our efforts may have some impact to consumer prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This highlights why careful deliberation by tripartite partners is necessary as we expand to more PWMs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: No company should unjustly profit from the PWM, but we must also recognise that these moves will not be without cost.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That is why Workfare continues to be important, as consumers and service buyers do not bear the cost impact of the wage supplements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: All of us have a role to play as our low-wage workers enjoy better wages, dignity and respect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I agree with Mr Raj Joshua Thomas that seeking the well-being of our fellow workers must be part of our culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government will partner the community in this effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With this in mind, the Workgroup has called for the formation of the Alliance for Action (Afa) for Lower-Wage Workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This Alliance for Action or AfA will mobilise passionate, action-oriented people to contribute to the whole-of-society effort to uplift low-wage workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government supports the Workgroup's call and we will launch the AfA soon and run co-creation workshops for AfA members over the next six months to start these ground-up initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, moving on to workplace safety, MOM is alarmed at the recent spate of workplace accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Ministry is investigating every incident and we call upon the whole industry to seriously review their safety protocols.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We acknowledge that companies are facing manpower shortages due to border and pandemic controls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Nevertheless, companies must not compromise worker safety by rushing or having workers operate machinery or perform tasks that they are not trained for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They should also review their risk assessments to account for COVID-19 conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since mid-December 2020, MOM has stepped up enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Out of 510 inspections since mid-December, MOM has uncovered 486 contraventions and issued seven Stop-Work Orders (SWOs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since last November, Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council and industry associations have called for two Safety Time Outs (STOs) to improve safety protocols.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are particularly concerned with the Tuas explosion on 24 February, resulting in multiple casualties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It was one of the worst accidents in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our inspectors have commenced inspections on close to 500 companies that may have combustible dust hazards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this is to ensure that risks are minimised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Minister for Manpower will appoint an Inquiry Committee to thoroughly study the case and recommend prevention measures, including policy or regulatory changes if necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about workplace safety amongst sub-contractors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Sub-contractors are not the only ones responsible for workplace safety and health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This way, developers and main contractors can make more informed decisions in appointing safer sub-contractors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We intend to expand this to other sectors for service buyers to influence WSH outcomes through their choice of contractors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In this way, safer companies will have better access to business opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope the private sector will follow suite in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This approach is an important complement to deterrent penalties in WSH prosecutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Based on MOM's inspections, almost all companies have appointed a Safe Management Officer (SMO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We support Mr Melvin Yong's suggestion that companies could consider upskilling their SMOs to become WSH representatives through courses such as the Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) Certificate in Workplace Safety and Health or through participating in the bizSAFE programme, for which training subsidies are available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore has come a long way in our workplace safety and health standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since the Nicoll Highway collapse in 2004, our workplace fatal injury rate reduced from 4.9 per 100,000 workers to 1.1 per 100,000 workers in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is a level achieved only by a handful of developed countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But still, we must never be complacent and we remain committed in our goal in making Singapore one of the safest workplaces in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic has reminded us of the importance of ensuring workforce and workplace resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For its part, the Government is committed to continue leading efforts to uplift our lower-wage workers, to ensure good workplace safety practices and to enhance employees' mental wellbeing, not just for the benefit of every worker but also for the good of employers and society-at-large.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The past year has not been easy for employers, employees and jobseekers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One group that is new to our workforce and learning to navigate their entrance into it are our recent graduates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the progress of our SGUnited Traineeships and its impact on our graduates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Not surprisingly, fewer graduates found permanent full-time employment last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I agree with Prof Hoon Hian Teck that our graduates on traineeship can gain industry-relevant experience and build their networks as pathways to future job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Most of these traineeships were in growth sectors such as financial services, information and communications, and professional services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This allows the programme to support the class of 2021 as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are making some adjustments to the SGUnited Traineeships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will raise training allowances for ITE and Polytechnic graduates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is to give an extra boost to our ITE and Polytechnic graduates, who are facing more difficulty in finding jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We hope that our recent graduates who have not been able to find jobs can seriously consider traineeships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The traineeships are available to graduates from the private education institutes as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Nadia Samdin will be pleased to know that we have made changes to facilitate trainees' transition into jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Companies will not be allowed to take on the same trainee for a second traineeship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We want to encourage host organisations to hire trainees who have performed well during the traineeship stint.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These changes will take effect on 1 April 2021. 2021 is a year of celebrating Singaporean women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I wholeheartedly support this initiative and I would like to take this opportunity to update on the employment of women in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our female employment rate has remained stable at 73% despite the impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This speaks to the strength and resilience of our women amidst challenging labour market conditions and reflects our efforts in supporting female employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if the practice of declaring the last drawn salary contributed to the gender pay gap.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He referred to a Boston University study on the impact of salary history on gender pay gap.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The United States introduced a salary history ban in 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In Singapore, the adjusted gender pay gap is about 6%, which is lower than that in the United States.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: According to a 2018 study by Assoc Prof Jessica Pan from NUS, occupational segregation was a key contributor to the gender wage gap here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In Singapore, jobseekers do not have to comply with requests for their last drawn salary and employers cannot insist on it either.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: If a jobseeker chooses to provide salary information, employers should use it carefully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I share Ms Mariam Jaafar's and Ms Yeo Wan Ling's conviction that we should support women to stay active in the labour force.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is perhaps a sign that more men are sharing in care-giving responsibilities at home and our workplaces have become more supportive of women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are mindful, however, that in our Asian culture, women carry a disproportionate weight in care-giving duties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In 2020, 65% of women who were outside the labour force cited family responsibilities as the main reason as compared to only 8% of men.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our answer to this is not in asking men to stay at home and be full-time care-givers but to increase support for care-givers as a whole so that they can contribute to work and have an income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I share Ms Carrie Tan's views on the importance of supporting care-givers in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We acknowledge that care-giver leave helps them take care of their loved ones through short-term illnesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: However, it is also important to hear from care-givers what is most helpful to them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our conversations with working care-givers showed that flexible work arrangements were more important and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We also support care-givers who would like to return to the workforce by providing career matching services from Workforce Singapore (WSG).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through providing a supportive environment for our working care-givers, we can empower them to fulfill career aspirations concurrently with family commitments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Lower wage care-givers who are working may also be eligible for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme, which provides up to $4,000 in cash and CPF top-ups annually.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have also taken steps to help care-givers build their retirement nest egg.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: First, we encourage cash top-ups to CPF accounts of care-givers through tax incentives and Government matching grants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Second, we supplement the retirement income of seniors who had low incomes during their working years through the Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Carrie Tan also suggested for us to combine childcare and parent care leave to form a more holistic family care leave provision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While we agree that this might provide more flexibility to care-givers who have to take care of both children and their parents, we will have to consider the long-term implications of such a measure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: COVID-19 has accelerated the adoption of flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Most companies implemented flexible work arrangements last year in view of safe management requirement for the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Many successfully redesigned work processes and infrastructure to facilitate staggered work hours and work-from-home arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Louis Chua and Mr Louis Ng would like to see flexible work arrangements continuing post-COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The importance of flexible work arrangements was echoed in the recent Emerging Stronger Conversation series too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Although COVID-19 has significantly increased the proportion of people working from home, further study is needed to understand the impact of such arrangements on the work productivity and wellbeing of employees in the long term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Some employers may feel that work-from-home, if protracted, could hinder collaboration, productivity and the building of team spirit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Some employees may prefer to work in the office if their home environment is not conducive or for social interaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The degree to which work-from-home can be proliferated will vary across occupations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will look at the experiences of other jurisdictions such as the UK and Australia, which have introduced flexible work arrangement legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: But we will need to work with our tripartite partners to ensure a holistic representation of employees and employers' interests as we decide on the steps for the longer term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have recently formed an Alliance for Action for Work-Life Harmony to help companies instill workplace practices and resources to promote work-life harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In the long term, this will help companies better attract and retain talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: At its heart, a progressive workplace is one where everyone is treated fairly and empowered to perform at their best.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There have been various calls by Members, including Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Louis Ng, to introduce additional legislation to tackle workplace discrimination and harassment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have laws to raise employment standards and we update them regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For harassment, we have the Protection from Harassment Act and the Penal Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These laws enable the Government to take action against harassers, including at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We can have more legislation to enforce against bad behaviour at the workplace but if we take a legal approach to every aspect of employment relations, we will have an adversarial industrial climate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Not legislating does not mean we do not have higher aspirations for our workforce and workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have Tripartite Guidelines, Advisories and Standards, and these have worked well in advancing both employers and employees' interests while maintaining a positive and constructive relationship between both groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Members may recall that before the Retirement and Re-employment Act was introduced, we also adopted a promotional approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to review this bag of tools and introduce and upgrade the tools as necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In about 50 cases each year, the employers were found to be in breach of the guidelines and had their work pass privileges suspended.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF), we encourage fair employment practices that are open and merit-based.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We hold employers to account for not considering the workforce in Singapore fairly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We proactively identify companies with suspicious workforce profiles, that is, companies that have an exceptionally high share of foreign professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) compared to their industry peers or a high concentration of a single foreign nationality source.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We place them on our FCF Watchlist for closer scrutiny of their hiring practices even if they have not flouted any rules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: More importantly, schemes like the Jobs Support Scheme, Jobs Growth Incentive and Professional Conversion Programme tilt the balance in favour of hiring locals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is similar to how we take a progressive approach to reducing other forms of workplace discrimination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Specifically for seniors, job redesign and reskilling have also enabled us to increase their employment in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Despite the absence of an age discrimination law, Singapore's senior employment rate increased from 59% to 67.5% in the past decade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In contrast, countries like the UK and US have age discrimination laws but lower senior employment rates than in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In short, we will use a range of tools as well as legal and regulatory measures to keep our workplaces progressive, fair and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, Singaporeans take pride in being a caring and kind society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We teach our children to take care of the vulnerable and disadvantaged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Many Singaporeans were outraged when we heard about what happened to Ms Piang Ngaih Don, a foreign domestic worker from Myanmar who was brutally abused by her employer and died tragically in 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We must do our best to support vulnerable groups such as the elderly, children and foreign domestic workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Foreign domestic workers play a key role in supporting our families, whether in household chores or care-giving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Most employers appreciate the help from their foreign domestic workers and build good relationships with them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: However, some employers treat their foreign domestic workers unreasonably.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers in Singapore must know that any abuse of foreign domestic workers will not be tolerated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: First, making greater use of existing touch points with foreign domestic workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employment agents should have an interest to ensure that the foreign domestic workers they place settle in well, especially those working in Singapore for the first time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Third, our partner organisations like CDE and FAST can also expand their outreach and engagement, to strengthen the network of support to foreign domestic workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These measures do not in any way, remove or reduce the responsibility of each employer to take care of his or her foreign domestic worker.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Neither can they eliminate completely the risk of foreign domestic worker abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: But we must do all we can to minimise its incidence, and build a culture of respect for foreign domestic workers, in our homes and in our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOM will provide an update in due course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to conclude in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: (In Mandarin):    Although we face many challenges, we will continue to work hard to build a fairer and more inclusive workplace for our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Regardless of gender, age, race or physical ability, we want to make sure that all Singaporeans are able to thrive at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Government, employers, workers and the community, can all do our part to protect the vulnerable in our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Let us work together and march towards a fairer and more cohesive society.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate MOM in highlighting that low-wage care-givers also get income top-ups through Workfare.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In my cut, however, I was calling specifically for attention to look into basic income for full-time stay home care-givers who were previously from hired and low-wage industries.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: By this I mean a community that has moved from low-wage, literally, to no wage.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am not sure whether this group of community is receiving enough attention because they may not fall conveniently within MOM's portfolio given that they are not in the workforce.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And, if so, can Minister of State or someone please share like which Ministry should we be directing the attention for this community of care-givers, to look out for their well-being and their interest because they do not fall conveniently within a particular portfolio.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: There are also various respite care options in eldercare centres and nursing homes for care-givers who need help with caring for seniors for short periods of time, including during the weekends.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Another example is the area of financial support.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: To answer Ms Carrie Tan's question, actually it is a whole-of-Government.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: There are several Ministries working together to support care-givers, whether they are full-time care-givers or part-time care-givers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We have the MSF that looks at ComCare.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We have MOH that looks at supplementing and providing alternative care-giver options.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And we have MOM as well that looks at CPF support and retirement savings support for care-givers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, I would not say that it is a single Ministry but rather, a whole-of-Government effort to support care-givers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First of all, I want to thank Minister for acknowledging the work of the Labour Movement and affirmation of the importance of tripartism.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Minister mentioned about the Jobs Transformation Map.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is an important evolution in our transformation journey.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Minister update which are these 12 industries or sectors that will be in the first phase of this transformation?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How many jobs are expected to be impacted and how can tripartite partners be part of this transformation?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How does the Minister see the role of such search firms vis-a-vis the current placement agencies such as WSG and e2i in the longer term development of job placement in Singapore?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Desmond Choo, the GPC Chair for his clarifications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think search firms and WSG as well as e2i, they play complementary roles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The search firms or, more broadly speaking, employment agencies have well established networks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They have within their networks companies whose recruitment requirements are well known to them because on an on-going basis, these employers reach out to the employment agents to help fill positions for a simple reason – they may not have a very large HR department with recruitment specialists.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the employment agencies have their own networks of hiring employers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The other benefits that I think the search firms and employment agencies bring is that quite often they guide the jobseekers on what aspects of their resume and skillsets ought to be emphasised when presenting themselves to the prospective employers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is very often the key deciding factor.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because of their in-depth knowledge of prospective employers' requirements, which sometimes go beyond what can be stated in a job advertisement, this insight enables the jobseekers to review their own set of experiences and profile themselves appropriately.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think in a well-developed landscape for job placement, the employment agencies can play a complementary role to WSG and with e2i.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think there is another value that they bring to the table and it is that quite often they will give very honest and direct feedback to the jobseekers and help them to appreciate where their chances might be better.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This message is better delivered through the employment agents, on some occasions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is a role for all the different parties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the question that Mr Choo asked on the Jobs Transformation Maps, it really depends on the sector – how many job roles will be identified systematically through the studies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: By the way, I should just add that not all of the sector agencies call them Jobs Transformation Maps.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We refer to them broadly as Jobs Transformation Maps because that is exactly what they help the companies and the individuals accomplish – jobs transformation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Whatever the sector agencies choose to call these studies, the key really is that when we speak very broadly about the impact of technology, we do not recognise sufficiently that the impact on specific industries and job roles depends very much on which technology we are talking about.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the case of financial services, three key technologies will have an impact – artificial intelligence (AI), robotic process, automation (RPA) and advanced analytics.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The study looks specifically at the impact of 121 job roles, arising out of these three technologies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
